sentences.text: Here is what nobody tells you about the dead.
They do not hunt.
They repeat.
They show up around seven.
They lean on the shutter all day long.
Around nine at night, they drift away.
They shop the way they always shopped.
Nights are quiet.
Nights were always quiet.
That is why you took this job.
So you keep to night hours.
After dark, the roof is yours.
You cook up there on a camping stove from aisle 11.
Never indoors.
In a sealed building, a gas flame can kill you more quietly than they ever could.
On day four, the taps run dry.
No power means no pumps.
Drinking is easy: you have eight pallets of bottled water.
The toilets are the problem.
So it is one bucket, one bin bag, and a trip to aisle 13 for cat litter.
Turns out it was useful after all.
On day five, a car rolls into the staff lot.
It stops perfectly between the lines.
It is Rhea's.
She sits behind the wheel with the engine running until the tank is empty.
She never gets out.
By day eight, the driver's door hangs open and the seat is empty.
On day nine, you are asleep on a pile of dog beds when the ceiling turns white.
Every light blazes and every freezer roars.
And out of every speaker, the store playlist at full volume.
The power is back.
Outside, 250 heads turn at once.
The main breaker sits in the back office, seventy yards away.
